The fix is ready! I've corrected the floating-point precision issue in both `src/money.js` and `src/locale.js` by wrapping the price-to-cents conversion with `Math.round()`. 

The problem was that multiplying floating-point numbers by 100 can produce imprecise results (e.g., `39.95 * 100` → `3995.0000000000005`), which failed the validation check that requires prices to be exact integers (whole cents).

I've verified the fix works:
- ✅ All 50 existing tests pass
- ✅ `subtrack add Gym 39.95` now works
- ✅ Existing prices like Netflix (12.99) and Spotify (10.99) still work
- ✅ Other problematic prices (14.95, 29.95, 49.95) also work
